Command: Stretch Out the Rod for the Plagues
Summary: God's repeated command through the plagues: Moses (and Aaron with the rod) must stretch out hand and rod over Egypt for each sign.
Commandment: Take thy rod, and stretch out thine hand upon the waters of Egypt, and over the signs that follow.
Scripture: Exodus 7:19; Exodus 8:5; Exodus 8:16; Exodus 9:22; Exodus 10:12; Exodus 10:21
Application: A merged row under the one-row-per-distinct-command rule: the rod is stretched out for blood (Exodus 7:19), frogs (8:5), lice (8:16), hail (9:22), locusts (10:12), and darkness (10:21) — one repeated commanded act across the plague series, not six separate laws. The Red Sea stretching is rowed separately because it is a different act with a different outcome. Parent may split per plague if finer granularity is wanted.
Purpose: To bring each plague as a sign against Pharaoh and the gods of Egypt until Israel was let go (Exodus 7:17; 8:10).
